about: andrey.notears against the authors' notears_linear and andrey.dagma against the authors' dagma package, on linear SEMs at the papers' densities, with the empty graph as the floor and R2-SortnRegress and Var-SortnRegress as sortability controls
build: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 on the 0.17.0 release branch (version string 0.16.0), commit 6a3b0a4b3

references.notears: the authors' notears_linear, xunzheng/notears at commit 4a9ab19f, lambda1 0.1, loss_type l2, w_threshold 0.3
references.dagma: the authors' package dagma 1.1.1, DagmaLinear(loss_type='l2').fit(X, lambda1=0.03), w_threshold 0.3

verdict_rule: Decision cells: the standardized ones, 24 per method (ER2 and SF4; 10, 20, 50, 100 variables; Gaussian, exponential, Gumbel noise; 20 datasets each, seeds 0-19). Per cell D = SHD(a) - SHD(b) per dataset on the datasets both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D over 10,000 resamples lies wholly above 0, better when wholly below, a tie otherwise; fewer than 10 pairs are not judged. Reference bar: no decision cell worse than the reference on the first seeds and again on seeds 20-39. Floor bar: the interval of SHD(Andrey) - SHD(empty graph) lies wholly below 0 in more than half of the decision cells. Both hold: the method meets the bar for supported. The floor fails: not supported, whatever the reference does. The rule was fixed before the run. The raw and rescaled cells, MEC SHD, the controls, and the robust arms are reported and do not decide.

repairs.note: cycle repairs of the references' thresholded outputs, counted by refitting the recorded datasets with the lane's calls, on other hosts of the same CPU model. Every refit of the authors' NOTEARS code returned its recorded graph; same_graph_as_recorded counts the refits of the authors' dagma that did, so its counts describe the refits. A repair drops the weakest edges, one at a time, until no cycle is left. Not refitted: the authors' NOTEARS code at 100 variables (standardized) and at 50 variables on the raw and rescaled scales.
